As of 230 PM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Scattered showers are possible on Thursday as a 
series of cold fronts approaches.

Afternoon sfc analysis depicted high pressure over the area with 
mostly sunny skies and temps as of 130 PM in the upper 60s to mid 
70s across most of the area and mid 60s across the Eastern Shore. 
Well to the west, a shortwave trough aloft was digging into western 
portions of the Midwest. Cloud cover increases tonight into Thursday 
morning as the shortwave approaches. Given partly cloudy skies 
tonight, lows will be "mild" in the mid-upper 40s for most of the 
area and lower 50s along the coast.

The shortwave moves into the local area Thursday morning, allowing 
for an increase in cloud cover as well as a few isolated to 
scattered light showers. The 12z HRRR and RRFS were in agreement 
regarding these morning showers with the initial shortwave. As such, 
have increased PoPs to 30-45% Thursday morning in a SW-NE 
orientation across the NW half of the FA. These showers will likely 
be light and brief with a break in the precip likely from mid-late 
morning into early afternoon on Thursday. Breaks in the cloud cover 
are expected behind the first round of showers. This will help 
temperatures to warm into the upper 60s to lower 70s with dew points 
in the low-mid 50s for most (locally upper 40s). Given the low dew 
points, instability is expected to remain low with around 500 J/kg 
of SBCAPE in the afternoon. However, given the strong trough over 
the area brining with it cool temps aloft, mid-level lapse rates 
increase to around 7 C/km (potentially up to 7.5 C/km for some). Low-
level lapse rates will be even higher with most models showing lapse 
rates of >9 C/km. These lapse rates combined with the afternoon 
clearing, a secondary piece of vorticity, and a cold front should 
allow for scattered afternoon showers to develop in the lee of the 
Appalachians and move east across the local area. The HRRR and RRFS 
both show this convection. As such, confidence has increased in 
afternoon showers. As such, have increased PoPs to 30-60% in the 
afternoon with the best chance north of US-460 in the mid-late 
afternoon. Additionally, while severe weather is not expected, gusty 
winds will likely accompany the stronger showers. Pea-sized hail and 
a few rumbles of thunder are even possible.

Any stronger showers should end quickly after sunset with the loss 
of diurnal instability. However, both the HRRR and RRFS show 
lingering, light stratiform precipitation (likely a combination 
of drizzle and light rain) continuing into Thursday night behind
the cold front. The best chance for this is across central VA. 
Any lingering showers likely end for most areas Thursday night 
with a few lingering showers possible across the Eastern Shore 
early Friday morning. While several rounds of showers are 
possible Thursday, overall rainfall totals are still expected to
remain light with <0.2" expected for most locations. Locally 
higher rainfall totals of 0.25-0.5" are possible across portions
of central VA where showers train over the same areas. Even so,
rainfall totals will be light. Unfortunately, this looks to be 
the last chance of rain over the next week or more.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Much cooler temperatures arrive Friday into early 
next week with below freezing overnight temperatures likely
inland.

The anomalously strong trough remains centered over the region 
through Saturday before gradually moving offshore. However, 
troughing will persist through at least early next week. As such, 
expect the coldest air of the season beginning Friday and continuing 
through early next week. Each night (beginning Friday night), 
widespread lows near or below freezing are expected inland with some 
locations dropping into the upper 20s a few nights. Therefore, 
widespread frost and freeze conditions are expected which will bring 
the end to the growing season for most locations away from the 
coast. A hard freeze (lows at or below 28F) is even possible for 
some. While the growing season has already ended for our Piedmont 
counties, Freeze Watches will likely be needed in future updates 
across most of the remaining inland areas for Friday night/Saturday 
morning. Near and along the coast, NW winds remain elevated enough 
to keep temperatures from cooling below freezing. Instead, lows in 
the upper 30s to lower 40s are expected for these areas. Highs each 
day from Friday through early next week likely remain in the 50s 
(low-mid 50s for most). However, cannot rule out a few locations 
struggling to reach above the upper 40s across far northern portions 
of the area (mainly the lower MD Eastern Shore) Friday and Saturday.

Additionally, NW winds will be breezy behind the cold front(s) with 
gusts up to 20-25 mph inland and 25-30 mph along the coast possible 
Friday and Saturday. While winds will diminish each night
